This document plans a tool that scaffolds the agent workflow (front-load context -> structured plan -> iterative and adversarial review -> isolated implementation -> adversarial review) into a project, so the structure does not have to be hand-rolled each time. It follows the same planning format the tool is meant to scaffold.

## Motivations

- Setting up the workflow by hand for each project is repetitive: the same planning-document skeleton, the same guidance/principles, the same reusable prompts, and (when wanted) the same worktree and container isolation.
- The setup should work in two modes: starting a new project, and adding to or editing an existing one. A greenfield-only template does not cover the second mode.
- The default should be minimal. Extra machinery (diagram prompt packs, container isolation, language starters) should be opt-in rather than imposed.
- Guidance should be harness-agnostic: `AGENTS.md` is the canonical file, with any harness-specific file (for example `CLAUDE.md`) reduced to a thin pointer to it.

These govern how this tool is built.

Note: the principles the tool _ships_ to other projects (the default `AGENTS.md` content) are a separate artifact from these; the shipped set and its data model are covered in the `core-assets` step and live in `pack/principles.toml`.

## Documentation Protocol

This plan is kept current during the work.

Progress lives in the Roadmap: an ordered table of step slugs and their status (`not started`, `in progress`, `complete`, `skipped`, `next`, `optional`, `deferred`, or `blocked on <slug>`). The Roadmap is the single source of truth for status and for implementation order. The Step Details below carry each step's design, decisions, and (once done) outcome and evidence, and do not repeat the status label.

Steps are identified by a stable kebab-case slug, not a number, so a reference stays valid when the order changes: every cross-reference to a step uses its slug. Each Roadmap row maps to a detail block headed by the same slug; some detail blocks are grouped under an umbrella heading that carries context shared by several steps, and the umbrella itself is not a Roadmap entry. To add a step, add its detail block and insert its slug into the Roadmap at the right position; to reorder or reprioritise, edit the Roadmap rows. Keep the two in sync: every Roadmap slug has a detail block and vice versa.

The "Open Questions, Decisions, Issues and Blockers" section is the single living human-decision queue (the model adopted in `human-review-queue`). Each item has a stable id, a one-line ask, a status (`open`, `decided -> folded into <slug>`, or `superseded`), and a context pointer into the step or ledger that carries the detail. Resolved items are marked resolved, not deleted, so the same question is not addressed twice; the adopted decision and its reasoning are folded into the relevant step, and the queue item points to that step. The orchestrator updates the queue at every checkpoint as a required step and pushes the open items to the human rather than waiting for the human to pull them.

## Repository Layout and Current Architecture

This section maps the code as built, so the plan can be resumed without prior conversation context. The code in the repository is the source of truth; this is an index into it. The completed steps carry the reasoning; this carries the shape.

Build, run, and verify (see `README.md` for full user-facing usage):

- Use `just build` / `just test` / `just clippy` / `just fmt`, or plain `cargo` inside `nix develop` (with direnv, run `direnv allow` once). The justfile wraps the Nix environment.
- Verification before each commit: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `nix fmt`, and all text ASCII-clean (no em-dashes, en-dashes, emoji, or other non-ASCII; use `->`, `>=`, `!=`).
- The binary is a plain Rust program (edition 2021, MSRV 1.88) that runs without Nix. Nix, just, and direnv are development conveniences only. Dependencies: `clap` (derive), `serde`, `toml`, `ratatui = "0.30"`, `include_dir`.

Directory layout:

- `src/` holds the binary crate: four modules described below.
- `pack/` is the built-in default pack: `pack.toml` (the manifest), `AGENTS.md`, `plan-template.md`, `principles.toml`, and `prompts/`. It is embedded into the binary at compile time with `include_dir`, and it also loads through the same manifest path as an external `--template` pack (the pack is dogfooded).
- `flake.nix`, `.envrc`, `justfile`, `rustfmt.toml` are the dev environment (fenix toolchain, treefmt formatters, recipes). `LICENSE` is Blue Oak Model License 1.0.0.

Modules and key types (all shipped and tested):

- `src/main.rs` (CLI and orchestration). `Cli` (clap derive) exposes `--output-dir`, `--force`, `--vcs <git|none>` (git by default), `--write`, `--dry-run` (conflicts with `--write`), `--principles`, `--principle-detail`, `--list-principles`, `--template <dir>`, and `--var key=value` (repeatable); there is no `-i` flag, the selector is the default on a terminal. `main` builds the active `manifest::PackSource` (the built-in pack, or a `--template` directory), parses `--var` into an overrides map, loads the active pack's principles via `pack_principles`, and resolves the selection. `use_selector` then decides the mode: the two-pane TUI opens when both stdin and stdout are terminals, there are principles to choose, and neither `--write` nor `--dry-run` was given; its Save modal is the write confirmation. Otherwise the run is non-interactive and writes only with `--write`. Either way `main` builds the asset set with `build_assets`, computes each asset's `Outcome` with `outcome_of` (read-only, for the plan preview), decides the `--vcs` action with `init_plan` (read-only; `inside_git_repo` skips when already inside a repository), prints the plan (the repository line first), and, when confirmed, runs `run_git_init` (shell out to `git init`) before writing the assets with `apply_asset`. `Outcome` is `Created`/`Refreshed`/`SkippedExisting`/`Overwritten`; `outcome_of` decides it without touching disk and `apply_asset` performs the write, so the preview never writes. `#[cfg(test)] scaffold` is a build-plus-write convenience for the drop tests. User errors print to stderr and exit 2.
- `src/pack.rs` (principle data and selection). `Principle { id, name, summary, rationale, tags, default_selected, default_order, references, related }`. `parse_principles(&str)` parses a principles TOML file. `resolve_selection(principles, spec)` implements the `--principles` token grammar (comma-separated `default` / `all` / `none` / `tag:<t>` / bare-id, de-duplicated by first occurrence; keyword and tag tokens expand in `default_order`, id lists keep their given order) and returns `SelectionError { UnknownId, UnknownTag }`. `Detail { Name, Summary, Full }` with `render_principles` renders the selected set as a numbered list. `default_principles` / `DEFAULT_PRINCIPLES_TOML` are `#[cfg(test)]` only, because production reads principles through the active pack source (see `pack_principles`).
- `src/manifest.rs` (the pack format and loader; the abstraction `optional-modules` builds on). `PackSource { Embedded(&Dir), Directory(PathBuf) }` with a public `read(rel)` and a private `manifest()`; `builtin()` returns the embedded pack. `Manifest { asset: Vec<AssetSpec>, var: Vec<VarSpec>, module: Vec<ModuleSpec> }` deserializes `pack.toml` and ignores unknown keys. `AssetSpec { source, dest, ownership, render, module: Option<String>, executable: bool }`, `VarSpec { name, default: Option<String>, module: Option<String> }`, `ModuleSpec { name, description, guidance: Option<String>, requires: Vec<String> }`, and `Ownership { Reference, Working }`. A `module = "<name>"` tag on an asset or var declares optional-module membership: untagged entries are core (always applied), tagged ones only when `--module <name>` selects that module; the `[[module]]` section is the authoritative set of known module names. `render(template, vars)` does minimal `{{key}}` substitution (unknown placeholders left as-is). `load(source, builtin_vars, overrides, selected_modules)` reads the manifest, filters out unselected modules' assets and vars, resolves the variable map with `resolve_vars` (built-in vars first, then each selected/core declared default, then `--var` overrides; the name `principles` is reserved), and returns `Vec<Asset { dest, contents, ownership }>` or `LoadError { Io, UndeclaredVar, MissingRequiredVar, ReservedVar, UnknownModule, UndeclaredModuleTag, UndeclaredModuleRequire, DuplicateModule }` (all exit 2). The reserved computed variables are `principles`, `instrument`, and `modules` (a pack may neither declare nor `--var`-set them). The `checks` module and the `agent-scaffold checks` / `scaffold --with-precommit-hook` surfaces live in `src/checks.rs` and `src/main.rs` (see the `optional-modules` step).
- `src/tui.rs` (the interactive selector; TEA-lite, functions not traits, where TEA is The Elm Architecture: a single state value, a pure `update` reducer, and a render function). The only public item is `run_selection(principles, initial_included, save_summary) -> io::Result<Option<Vec<usize>>>`, which returns the chosen principle indices in order, or `None` on abort. Internally: one `App` value; `enum Mode { Editing, Filtering, Confirming { button } }`; `enum Event { Key, Resize }`; a pure `update(&mut App, Event) -> Step` reducer (`Step` is `Continue`/`Confirm`/`Abort`); a `ui` render function; and a blocking `run` loop over `next_event()` (the single seam where a concurrent event source could later be merged). No async, no custom traits. Key bindings are documented in the `selection-ui` step.

Pack format (the contract shared by the built-in pack and `--template` packs):

- A pack is a directory containing `pack.toml` plus the source files it references. External packs are passed with `--template <dir>`.
- `pack.toml` has `[[asset]]` entries `{ source, dest, ownership = "reference"|"working", render = true|false, module?, executable? }` (one source may map to several assets; `render` and `executable` default to false; `executable = true` drops the file with its executable bit set, for example a hook script) and optional `[[var]]` entries `{ name, default?, module? }` (an absent `default` makes the variable required), plus optional `[[module]]` entries `{ name, description, guidance?, requires? }` declaring the opt-in modules (`guidance` names a partial concatenated into `{{modules}}` when the module is enabled; `requires` lists modules it auto-enables).
- Optional modules: an asset or var with a `module = "<name>"` tag is dropped or required only when that module is selected with the repeatable `--module <name>` flag; untagged entries are core (always applied), so with no module selected the output is byte-identical to the core. Every module a tag references (and every `--module`) must be declared in a `[[module]]` section, and module names must be unique; a dangling tag, an unknown `--module`, or a duplicate declaration is an error and nothing is written.
- `ownership = "reference"` assets (conventionally under `.agents/`) are always (re)written; `ownership = "working"` assets are created only if absent, unless `--force`.
- `render = true` applies `{{name}}` substitution. `{{principles}}` and `{{instrument}}` are reserved, tool-computed variables (the rendered principle selection, and the instrumentation block when `--instrument` is set); a pack may neither declare nor `--var`-set either. Other variables come from `[[var]]` defaults, overridden by `--var key=value`; setting an undeclared variable, or leaving a required one unset, is an error and nothing is written. Every rendered asset is normalised to end with exactly one trailing newline, so an unused reserved placeholder leaves no trailing blank lines and the off output is byte-identical without relying on a formatter.
- A pack that ships `principles.toml` has its principles drive selection, `--list-principles`, the interactive selector, and `{{principles}}`; a pack without one simply has no principles to select. A pack may likewise ship an `instrument.md` render fragment, which is inlined into `{{instrument}}` when `--instrument` is set; this fragment is a special source read directly (like `principles.toml`), NOT a manifest `[[asset]]`, so it is not dropped as its own file. A pack without one renders `{{instrument}}` empty.

One run's data flow: parse CLI, build the `PackSource`, read and parse the pack's `principles.toml`, `resolve_selection` (or the interactive TUI) chooses and orders principles, `render_principles` produces the `{{principles}}` value, `manifest::load` resolves the variables and reads/renders each asset, `outcome_of` computes each asset's plan outcome, and, once writing is confirmed, `apply_asset` drops each honouring ownership and `--force`.

This section is the single living human-decision queue for the task (the model adopted in `human-review-queue`). Each item has a stable id, a one-line ask, a status, and a context pointer into the step or ledger that carries the detail. Statuses are `open` (awaiting a human decision), `decided -> folded into <slug>` (resolved; the decision and reasoning live in that step, and the item stays here marked resolved so it is not re-addressed), or `superseded` (replaced by a later item, kept for provenance). The orchestrator maintains this queue under the push-at-checkpoint rule stated in the Documentation Protocol; a folded decision reopens only on evidence that beats its recorded reasoning.

Historical note: the `OQ-<letter>` labels (OQ-A .. OQ-K) elsewhere in this plan are provenance markers for questions resolved and folded before this queue existed, not live entries; a reference such as "from OQ-E" points to a decision now recorded inline in the relevant step. The pre-queue questions were: OQ-B/C/D (selection-polish), resolved in the TUI-polish steps; OQ-E (manifest and dogfooding), OQ-F (schema and variables), OQ-G (embedding), OQ-I (variable declaration schema), OQ-J (principle source under `--template`), resolved in the bring-your-own-template steps; OQ-H (git-URL fetch), deferred to `git-url-fetch`; OQ-K (version-control init), folded into `init-vcs`; plus the earliest questions (tool form, ownership and update model, principle set and data model, non-interactive selection UI, interactive TUI design), resolved in earlier steps and the code. The live queue below uses `Q-<n>` ids.

## Project Principles

1. Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff - prioritise correctness, internal coherence, and maintainability, and when a local fix conflicts with a cleaner design, choose the cleaner design unless a concrete limitation prevents it.
2. Minimal by default - The core does one thing well; everything else is an optional module the user opts into. Adding a module must not complicate the core.
3. Safe on existing projects - Scaffolding into a populated repo must never clobber or silently overwrite existing files. Prefer create-if-absent, namespaced locations, and clearly marked idempotent edits.
4. Idempotent - Running the tool twice produces the same result as running it once, with no duplicated blocks and no drift.
5. Make illegal states unrepresentable - Work out the valid inputs and outcomes first and encode them, rather than admitting bad states and guarding against them at runtime.
6. Ground decisions in evidence - Before an approach is built out, validate it with a small proof-of-concept that builds and produces the expected output. If the candidates are exhausted, raise the impasse for a decision rather than forcing through an unvalidated approach.
7. Reproducible - Prefer the project's existing toolchain conventions (Nix, just, direnv) so a scaffolded project and its checks behave the same on any machine.
8. Structured data first, project for humans - Prefer machine-readable structured formats as the single source for the data the workflow operates on (plan status, the decision queue, decisions/receipts, relationships, metrics), and derive human-readable views by projection, rather than hand-authoring prose that is also the machine input. At this pre-adoption stage, prioritise the best long-term design, architecture, and implementation over backwards-compatibility, API stability, or minimal-diff blast radius; those become constraints once the project has adoption and stability guarantees. Decided by the human 2026-07-18; when this conflicts with Principle 2 (minimal) or Principle 3 (safe on existing projects) at this stage, this wins, and it sharpens Principle 1 (cleaner long-term architecture) and Principle 16-equivalent one-source-of-truth thinking.

Trade-off: a token win only where the source grows unbounded or is re-read (the ledger especially), against per-call and per-turn overhead that can exceed a single file read for small files, plus a projection-drift risk (mitigated by the existing structural validator). - `Q-29` (decided -> folded into `exploration-mode`) first-class support for design-space exploration / deliberation: the workflow handles deciding (the `deliberation-mode` human-input contract) and deferring (an item stays `open`) a decision, but has no first-class mode for exploring a design space BEFORE options are decidable, which is what the human asked for on `Q-27`/`Q-28`. Decided (human, 2026-07-16, after the two-explorer design pass): add all four, low-ceremony, mostly docs plus one code line: an `exploring` Open-Questions status (in `plan.rs`), a design-notes artifact convention at `docs/plans/<task>.explorations/<question>.md` (parallel to `.reviews/`) whose shape is the human-input contract written to a file, design-exploration as a named intake mode in `AGENTS.md`, and an optional light review of an exploration (the multi-independent-explorer-plus-orchestrator-synthesis setup that produced this very decision is the review analog). Same "structure over disposition" root cause as `Q-27`/`Q-28`. Folded into `exploration-mode` (built first, being the cheapest and unblocking proper deliberation).

- `Q-34` (decided -> folded into `round-log-core`) unify round/review data on the JSONL log (single source of truth, comprehensive): evidence found while scoping `ledger-parse` (2026-07-16): structured per-round data is DUPLICATED across the ledger's `## Round summaries` table (stale at 2 rows) and the metrics JSONL (comprehensive, 52 rows, richer: `risk_class`, reviewer attribution, severities, `ts`, cross-task), violating single-source (Principle 16). DIRECTION DECIDED (human, Approach 1): promote `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` to the always-present structured workflow ROUND LOG (round logging becomes core, not opt-in), REMOVE the ledger's round-summary and findings-index tables (the ledger keeps only the Round-records narrative + RESUME STATE), and have convergence accounting, `workflow-invariants`, and `state-queries` all read the JSONL; per-finding detail stays in the review files (git history). This REOPENS folded decisions (`instrument-flag` `Q-4`/`Q-5`/`Q-6` the `--instrument` opt-in gate; `ledger-template` `Q-2`/`Q-3` the tables; `convergence-accounting` `Q-1` counting from the ledger; `Q-24` metrics validation now core) and re-scopes `ledger-parse` (down to a RESUME-STATE text extract, likely folded into `state-queries`) and `workflow-invariants` (reads the JSONL). A DESIGN PASS is owed (human-chosen) to pressure-test Approach 1 and produce the concrete MIGRATION plan: the `--instrument` disposition (drop vs repurpose), the always-on round-log rendering (the `instrument.md` fragment becomes core AGENTS.md content), the ledger-template edits, the convergence-accounting doc change, which existing steps reopen and in what order to keep the repo green, and the (minimal) data migration since the 52-record JSONL already covers all rounds. Decided (human, 2026-07-17): add an optional `harness` string to each `reviewers[]` element, before any cross-harness work. Decision and reasoning in `reviewer-harness-field`.
- `Q-38` (decided -> folded into `optional-modules`) seed a ripgrep ASCII check and dogfood ASCII enforcement: the checks module's seeded ast-grep rule cannot express this project's ASCII-clean convention (ast-grep rules must match AST kinds, not raw bytes), so a text/regex tool is needed. Decided (human, 2026-07-18): (a) NOW, ship a COMMENTED ripgrep `ascii-clean` example row in the seeded `checks.toml` (a non-ast-grep text/regex linter forbidding non-ASCII bytes, demonstrating the plug-in story and giving the ASCII recipe without imposing it on unicode-using projects); done in `optional-modules` increment 2b alongside a commented `ruff`+`paths` polyglot example. (b) DEFERRED to AFTER increment 2c: fully dogfood ASCII enforcement in agent-scaffold itself by adopting the checks module (`scaffold-self --module checks`) with an ACTIVE ripgrep ASCII row, once the `checks` subcommand exists to run it. Tracked as a post-2c action.
- `Q-39` (decided -> folded into `optional-modules`) format-check execution and isolation under the checks module: treefmt v2 (this project's `nix fmt`) has NO non-mutating dry-run, so a `kind = "format"` check via `--fail-on-change` FORMATS IN PLACE then reports; this would mutate the user's working tree (and, in a pre-commit hook, risk clobbering unstaged changes). 2b corrected the WORDING (the checks-reviewer authors only findings; a format check on an in-place formatter mutates a discardable copy). DECIDED (human, 2026-07-18): the `agent-scaffold checks` subcommand runs the checks in a SEPARATE, TEMPORARY git worktree (never the live tree), removed when the run finishes (including on failure/interrupt), so the current tree is never clobbered. This makes in-place format checks safe and matches the project's git-is-the-recovery-substrate and writer-isolation model. Content selection: a plain `checks` run isolates the current WORKING-TREE state (e.g. via a `git stash create` commit of the dirty state, or HEAD when clean); `checks --staged` isolates the STAGED/index content (e.g. a tree written from the index), so the pre-commit hook checks exactly what will be committed without touching unstaged work. Implementation plumbing (git primitives, edge cases: empty repo, no commits, clean tree) is worked out in 2c and verified by its risky review loop.
- `Q-40` (decided -> folded into `waiver-model`) representing a human-authorized convergence below the required clean-round streak so `validate --workflow` (W3) does not false-flag it: DECIDED (human, 2026-07-18) the escalation-record-aware approach (W3 accepts an increment's recorded streak when its records carry a `type:"escalation"` `human_decision:"decision"` record; reuses existing log data, no new schema/status, scoped and auditable). RESOLVED and built in `waiver-model` (2026-07-18): the escalation-record-aware idea was refined into the unified waiver, an explicit `accepted-at-escalation` `record-backed` `type:"waiver"` record whose `evidence` W5 validates against the increment's real `type:"escalation" human_decision:"decision"` record (rather than W3 silently auto-accepting on escalation presence), so the exemption is a declared, unit-scoped, auditable log line. Decision and outcome are in the `waiver-model` Step Detail. `optional-modules` increment 2c-ii was RISKY (its review found three high-severity write-escapes) but converged at ONE clean round, not two, because at the 5-round total-cap the human decided (per the escalation contract) to accept it, the dangerous write-escape class being closed and independently confirmed. Its round records are therefore risky with a peak `consecutive_clean` of 1, which W3 (risky requires peak >= 2) will flag as non-converged when `optional-modules` is eventually marked `complete` (after increment 3). Neither `trivial` nor `grandfathered` fits (it is neither review-skipped nor pre-logging). MUST be resolved before `optional-modules` is marked complete. Candidate approaches to bring to the human: an escalation-decision-aware exemption in W3 (a `type:"escalation"` record with `human_decision:"decision"` for the increment authorises its recorded streak); a per-increment override marker/status; or record the human-accepted lower streak as an explicit accepted-risk annotation W3 reads. Related to the severity-trajectory convergence idea recorded in `workflow-calibration`. This gap was surfaced by this very session's dogfooding (the meta-value of the workflow reviewing itself).
- `Q-41` (decided -> folded into `optional-modules`) `optional-modules` increment 3 (the isolation module) concrete file shape: the DIRECTION is already decided (pointer-scaffolding, not real container integration; `Q-33`/`Q-36`, design record `docs/plans/cross-harness-isolation.explorations/q33-q36-{A,B}.md`), but the step detail owes "its own design pass" on the exact integration shape, which files the `--module isolation` bundle drops and how they point a project at agent-box (`https://github.com/0xferrous/agent-box`) and agent-images (`https://github.com/nothingnesses/agent-images`) for worktree/container writer-agent isolation. A design pass is owed; the item points at `docs/plans/optional-modules-inc3.explorations/`. Grounding for the pass: the checks module (increment 2) is the template for how a content module lives in the pack (a `[[module]]` with a `guidance` partial rendered into `{{modules}}`, plus module-tagged assets, create-if-absent working files vs reference files); agent-box uses a global `~/.agent-box.toml` plus `ab spawn --local` and `ab new`/`ab spawn -s <session> --git` (worktree mode) over agent-images OCI images. The deferred growth path (a `.agents/spawn.toml` role->launch map + an agent-box container-wrapper shim) is already recorded in the step detail and stays deferred; this pass settles only the pointer-scaffolding content that ships now. Design pass DONE (two explorers, `docs/plans/optional-modules-inc3.explorations/isolation-module-shape-{A,B}.md`). Both converge on the skeleton: one `[[module]] isolation` entry with `guidance = "isolation-guidance.md"` and no `requires` (orthogonal to checks), one guidance partial `pack/isolation-guidance.md` rendered into `{{modules}}` (points at the `agent-isolation` rule for the tier policy, supplies only the container-tier wiring: agent-images `nix build`/`podman load`, the global `~/.agent-box.toml` shape, the `ab new`/`ab spawn --git` worktree flow, and preflight detection), byte-identical when off, no runtime dependency, no shelling out. They DIFFER on ONE point, the open decision: whether to ALSO drop a project-local working file `.agents/isolation/README.md` (create-if-absent). Explorer A (minimalism/safety): NO, guidance-only, because agent-box config is a per-user GLOBAL file so there is nothing project-local to own and a dropped README duplicates the partial's content (drift, Principle 16); zero clobber surface (Principle 3). Explorer B (reproducibility): YES, one lean working file recording WHICH image the project uses (e.g. claude-code vs codex), a project-level fact captured nowhere else in the repo, so setup is not tribal knowledge (Principle 7). DECIDED (human, 2026-07-18): Option A, GUIDANCE-ONLY, no dropped file. Rationale: agent-box config is a per-user global file so there is nothing project-local to own; the one project-level fact (image choice) is thin and a scaffolded template risks an empty stub or duplicating the partial (Principle 16); it is the safest shape (Principle 3, zero clobber surface) and lands the setup where the orchestrator already reads it at preflight (Principle 1). Folded into the `optional-modules` increment-3 step detail.
- `Q-42` (decided -> folded into `decision-receipt`) a checkable receipt that the human-input contract was presented at every human-decision point: the human observed (2026-07-18) that the `Q-40` decision was acceptable because they were presented the options, trade-offs, a recommendation, and principle-judged reasoning before deciding, and asked that the workflow GUARANTEE this every time a human decides, with a durable receipt/proof that it happened. The human-input-contract RULE already requires this presentation; what is missing is a checkable receipt and enforcement (the same rule-then-detection pattern `workflow-invariants`/W3 applied to convergence). Partial receipts already exist (`type:"escalation"` and `type:"intake"` records; decided Open-Questions items folded into steps), so this generalises them. Key design nuance for genuine PROOF vs orchestrator self-attestation: the strongest receipt records the OPTIONS PRESENTED plus the human's SELECTION among them (choosing option Y from {X,Y,Z} inherently proves {X,Y,Z} was shown), rather than a self-certified "I presented the contract" flag. Candidate approaches to weigh: (a) a new `type:"decision"` JSONL receipt (question id, options presented, recommendation, human's choice) plus a `validate --workflow` check (a W4 analog) that every `decided` queue item has a matching receipt, coherent with the round-log/ledger split (Principle 16 with the accepted round-vs-narrative duplication, Principle 6 checkable); (b) a lighter in-queue standard: every `decided` item must carry the presented options + the choice inline, with a completeness check over the prose (less machinery, weaker check); (c) rely on git history + the existing escalation/intake records + AskUserQuestion structured answers, no new mechanism (Principle 2 minimal, but no deterministic proof, under-delivers on the ask). COUPLES to `escalation-exempt` (`Q-40`): escalation acceptance is itself a human decision that would carry a receipt, and both make W3 read human-decision records, so `escalation-exempt`'s build is held until this path is chosen so the two are designed coherently. The design space is genuinely open (receipt form, which decision points are covered, what makes proof genuine, whether to enforce), so a design pass (explorers) is a candidate before deciding. Trade-off the human should weigh: accountability/auditability of the decision process vs ceremony added to every decision point (Principle 2). A DESIGN PASS is owed (human-directed, 2026-07-18); the item points at `docs/plans/decision-receipts.explorations/`. The human is unclear on four things the pass must answer head-on: (1) the PURPOSE and what it AFFORDS the workflow (for whom, and what auditability of the decision process actually buys); (2) the TRADE-OFFS (the Principle 2 ceremony cost vs the benefit); (3) what it would concretely LOOK LIKE (form, where it lives, the check); and (4) how it RELATES to the plan, especially the Open Questions section and Principle 16 (single source of truth), is a receipt a duplicate of the decided queue item (an SSOT violation) or a genuinely distinct thing (the ATTESTATION that the contract-shaped presentation happened, vs the queue which holds the decision CONTENT). FIXED CONSTRAINT handed to the pass (established in deliberation, not re-open): receipts do NOT live in the ledger, because the ledger is per-task and DELETED at task close while decisions are permanent, and most decisions happen outside any review loop where no ledger exists; the ledger only narrates a mid-loop decision (a cap escalation, an accept-risk) as a POINTER to the durable receipt/queue, exactly today's escalation pattern. The NULL option (existing machinery, the Open Questions queue + `type:"escalation"`/`type:"intake"` records + git history + structured AskUserQuestion answers, already suffices, build nothing or only a light check) is a first-class candidate the pass must genuinely weigh, not a strawman. DESIGN PASS DONE (two explorers, `docs/plans/decision-receipts.explorations/receipt-system-{A,B}.md`; A skeptical/minimalist recommends NULL, B architect/steelman recommends the FULL receipt). They AGREE on three things that narrow the choice: (i) the LIGHT option (a prose-completeness check on queue items) is rejected by BOTH (a structural check over free prose parses at the wrong boundary, Principle 14, and is weaker than it looks); (ii) the CEILING, no orchestrator-authored artifact is adversarial PROOF, only auditable evidence, since the same orchestrator writes both the presentation and the receipt (the same ceiling W3 already accepts); the only truly unforgeable evidence is the human's own AskUserQuestion selection, which lives in the transcript/git outside the workflow artifacts; (iii) `escalation-exempt` (`Q-40`) is UNBLOCKED either way, it reads the existing `type:"escalation"` record for its W3 exemption regardless of this decision, and a decision receipt (if built) is a separate record for a separate check. So the real choice is a clean binary. FULL (B): a permanent `type:"decision"` JSONL record (`q_id`, `options`, `recommendation`, `chosen` with the validator enforcing `chosen` is a member of `options`, `ts`) written when a queue item goes `decided`, plus a W4 `validate --workflow` check that every `decided` item has a matching receipt (forward-looking, historical Q-1..Q-41 exempt). Genuineness comes from the options-on-record + `chosen in options`; SSOT resolved as queue=CONTENT (what/why) vs receipt=PROCESS ATTESTATION (options+choice), q_id-linked, the same accepted split as the ledger-narrative vs JSONL-round-record. NULL (A): build nothing; a well-formed `decided` queue item ALREADY records options+recommendation+choice+reasoning in prose (`Q-41` is the existence proof), so a JSONL receipt is a SECOND permanent hand-authored home for the option-labels+choice -> Principle 16 drift with only a soft resolver; and since the orchestrator authors both, the receipt is no more trustworthy than the queue it duplicates, so it fails Principle 3 (no motivating incident; adds no independent trust). A's crux: W3's justification does NOT transfer, W3 guards a SILENT unsupervised skip, but a human is PRESENT at every decision, so a missing presentation is not silent. Optional A add-on: one AGENTS.md sentence making "a `decided` item records the options presented and the human's choice inline" the item standard, no new machinery. Orchestrator recommendation: leaning FULL (B) with A's constraints folded in (record only option LABELS + choice, never the reasoning, so the duplication is bounded and the queue stays authoritative for content; frame it honestly as enforced auditability, NOT proof), because the project's own revealed philosophy is enforce-over-trust (W3, the metrics validator, the drift guards, the ASCII check all exist for exactly this) and the human asked for a checkable guarantee; the honest counterweight is A's permanent-double-authoring SSOT cost and that the receipt cannot prove presentation, only that a structured record exists. NOTE for whoever builds it: B's document is internally inconsistent on whether to add `q_id` to `escalation`/`intake` records (its main text says add it; its YAGNI says do not and keep them separate); resolve toward KEEPING them separate (one purpose per record, Principle 16), a `decided` queue item gets its own decision receipt. HUMAN CHOSE FULL over NULL (2026-07-18): build a checkable decision receipt. BUT the human then noticed the SSOT hole A poked (a JSONL receipt is a second permanent home for the option-labels+choice) and proposed encoding the receipt as STRUCTURED DATA projected into the human-readable plan, so it is single-sourced. - `Q-51` (decided -> folded into `workflow-driver`) encode the workflow itself as a deterministic state-machine DRIVER (not just a post-hoc checker) to combat AGENT DRIFT as the workflow grows and accrues detail (agents forget to apply rules): the human proposed (2026-07-19) making `agent-scaffold` a Mealy-machine REPL that the orchestrator (or any agent/human) runs to keep driving the loop. It would (a) parse the current codebase + plan/ledger/metrics state into valid internal control states, (b) print a summary of the current state, the valid transitions it can take, and CRUCIALLY the next INSTRUCTION PROMPT for the agent (the role prompt with context filled in) based on that state, plus periodic reminders (for example the Project Principles). Documentation instructs agents to run it to receive further instructions, so the control flow lives in a deterministic program rather than in fallible agent memory. This is the natural third stage of the structured-data direction (structured SOURCE `plan.toml` -> structured ENFORCEMENT `validate --workflow` -> structured DRIVING, this idea) and builds directly on the machine-readable plan the `structured-skeleton` initiative just delivered. ORCHESTRATOR REFRAMING (to weigh in the design pass): it is not one global Mealy machine but a FLEET of per-unit control FSMs (one per active step / increment / review loop), the tool tracking the set and emitting the next instruction for each READY unit, and also acting as a DEPENDENCY SCHEDULER over the plan's `blocked_by` DAG (computing what may run in parallel now); the tool must own only CONTROL transitions and consume agent/human JUDGMENT as inputs (a triage verdict, a human decision, a commit), never make the judgments itself (get that boundary wrong and it either straitjackets or hallucinates decisions). HUMAN'S CONCERNS to resolve: (1) interaction with the writer-isolation tiers (orthogonal: the tool instructs, the orchestrator isolates; the tool reads durable state on main and can emit the resolved tier as part of the instruction); (2) parallel steps (the per-unit-FSM fleet + dependency scheduling above); (3) concrete inputs and outputs (candidate: input = the durable state plus event-recording subcommands like `record-round --outcome clean` that append the log AND advance state atomically, Principle 13; output = a per-unit state summary + valid transitions + the filled next-instruction prompt + Principle reminders, as JSON and human text; keep it STATELESS, recompute from the files each call so it survives crashes/compaction); (4) what is missing. ADDITIONAL CONSIDERATIONS the orchestrator raises for the pass: the tool would become the SOURCE of the workflow LOGIC (convergence/sequencing move from AGENTS.md prose into Rust), the strongest anti-drift property but the biggest cost, and the prose and code could themselves drift unless the AGENTS.md workflow section is GENERATED from the machine definition (the same render closure just built for the plan); ESCAPE HATCHES for exceptions and human overrides are mandatory or the tool becomes a cage; ADOPTION should be EVIDENCE-FIRST (Principle 6), start ADVISORY (the agent drives, the tool suggests, measure whether drift drops) then deepen to authoritative driving, mirroring the receipt/waiver pilots; and this OVERLAPS the queued drift-mitigation cluster (the re-grounding + provenance step and the `Q-50` doc-currency core guidance), so the pass must weigh whether the driver SUBSUMES them. This is a MAJOR initiative, larger than `structured-skeleton`, and genuinely design-open, so it is `exploring`: the human directed (2026-07-19) queueing the exploration FIRST, before folding the Q-50 / re-grounding work it overlaps. A multi-explorer design pass is owed (candidate lenses: a formal-FSM + concurrency model; the tool-vs-prose single-source boundary + AGENTS.md generation; the I/O contract + isolation/harness integration + advisory-first adoption; and a YAGNI/skeptic lens weighing the state-machine driver against the lighter drift mitigations), synthesised, then moved to `open` with options for the human. Design record: `docs/plans/mealy-workflow-driver.explorations/`. DESIGN PASS DONE (2026-07-19): four independent explorers (fsm-concurrency, tool-vs-prose, io-contract-and-adoption, yagni-skeptic) synthesised in `synthesis.md`. STRONG CONVERGENCE: build the ADVISORY MVP first (a read-only, stateless `agent-scaffold next` reusing the W3/W4/W5 reconstruction already shipped, largely the already-planned `state-queries` step plus a next-action reminder), DEFER the full driver (per-unit FSM fleet, `blocked_by` scheduler, event-recording write-path, AGENTS.md-from-machine generation, authoritative driving) behind an EVIDENCE GATE, single-source the convergence CONSTANTS to close the existing `required_streak`/AGENTS.md duplication, and treat the driver as COMPLEMENTING (not subsuming) the re-grounding step and Q-50 (un-gate those; Q-50 is a prerequisite if the driver is built). Options for the human: (A) build the advisory MVP evidence-gated [all four explorers recommend]; (B) build the full driver now [rejected as premature, a subsystem larger than structured-skeleton hardening an evolving workflow]; (C) do not build, rely on the lighter drift mitigations. Orchestrator recommendation: (A). HUMAN DIRECTION (2026-07-19): go with the FULL DRIVER (Option B) as the TARGET, but a DEEPER design pass is owed FIRST, brainstorm the design space, requirements, scope, and possible user flows before committing to a build, so this stays `exploring` (a second design pass owed, not yet decided). Orchestrator note carried into that pass (honouring the skeptic's main objection while enabling the full driver): keep the workflow LOGIC DATA-DRIVEN (a spec the tool interprets, not hardcoded Rust) so the workflow can still evolve without heavy code churn, and STAGE the build (the advisory tier is the natural first increment on the path to the full driver, reusing the W3/`state-queries`/`render` machinery). On synthesis, present a fuller design + a concrete staged build plan for the human to refine, then decide with a receipt. DESIGN SHAPE DECIDED (2026-07-19): ORQ-1 terminal authority = ADVISORY + validated event-RECORDING, NON-BLOCKING in-loop, with an OPT-IN boundary gate (`validate --workflow --strict` in CI or a pre-commit hook, reusing the checks/hook pattern) for hard enforcement at the LANDING boundary (this also answers ORQ-2: gate at the boundary, not per-step, keeping the loop robust, harness-agnostic, least-authority, and Q-24-respecting). ORQ-5 (reminder cadence): light, each `next` surfaces only the reminders relevant to the current action. READY TO FOLD: a `workflow-driver` staged umbrella (Stage 0a the `workflow.toml` control-constants spec + single-source the convergence constants into W3, closing the `required_streak`/AGENTS.md duplication; 0b generate the AGENTS.md control fragment from the spec, byte-guarded; 1 the advisory read-only `next` MVP, ~the planned `state-queries` + a next-action reminder; 2 type the `src/driver/` FSM engine with a shared reconstructor; 3+ the `blocked_by` scheduler, generation-widening, the guarded `record-*` write-path [reopens Q-24], and the opt-in authoritative boundary gate, all evidence-gated) carrying the decided design (data-driven-constants spec + Rust transition function; the projection-family framing where `validate`=backward, `status`=summary, `next`=forward, `render`=prose; the control-vs-judgment boundary enforced by types; semi-authoritative non-blocking recording). - `Q-52` (decided -> folded into `code-value-audit-static`) a deterministic, statistical-evidence-backed way to determine whether code is EARNING ITS KEEP (useful and worth keeping) vs accrued cruft/maintenance burden, run periodically (manually or in the workflow, e.g. at the acceptance/UAT step), likely MULTIPLE methods working together: the human raised (2026-07-19) that AI-accelerated development accrues code and maintenance burden faster, making keep-or-cut discipline the bottleneck, and asked for the prior art and how to OBJECTIVELY determine code usefulness. ORCHESTRATOR STARTING ANSWER (to be verified and extended by a WebSearch-backed research pass, since knowledge has a cutoff): usefulness is not intrinsic but RELATIONAL, made objective by making it FALSIFIABLE, the direct analog of mutation testing (mutation asks 'if I change this, does a test catch it?'; usefulness asks 'if I REMOVE this, does anything observably notice?'). Operational definition: code earns its keep iff removing it causes an observable loss (a test fails, the build breaks, a downstream dependency breaks, a production metric/behavior changes, or a documented requirement / public-API contract is violated). PRIOR-ART CLUSTERS to survey and cite: (1) static unused-code/reachability detection (compiler/linter dead-code, call-graph, `cargo-udeps`/`cargo-machete`, vulture, staticcheck, Knip, tree-shaking), blind to reflection/FFI/dynamic-dispatch/public-API; (2) dynamic/production usage (coverage as necessary-not-sufficient, PRODUCTION coverage / 'dark code' sampling, feature-usage telemetry tying code to user value); (3) DEBLOATING research (CHISEL, RAZOR, TRIMMER, piecewise compilation; delta-debugging / 1-minimality, Zeller), operationalizing keep-what-observed-use-needs; (4) mutation testing and its INVERSE, 'pseudo-tested methods' (Niedermayr et al.: body-nulling survives all tests -> effectively untested/weak-value), generalizable to a DELETION experiment; (5) behavioral-code-analysis / maintenance-cost hotspots (Tornhill/CodeScene churn x complexity, Feathers), the burden side; (6) traceability/provenance (code mapping to no requirement/test/API contract is suspect; connects to this repo's provenance direction). MULTI-SIGNAL DESIGN to propose: combine reachable/depended-on? (static) + exercised? (coverage) + deletion-safe? (deletion/pseudo-test mutant survives tests + canary, the strong signal) + traceable? (requirement/API contract; public API a legit keeper) + cost>value? (hotspot) into an ADVISORY report of candidates-not-earning-their-keep with per-signal evidence, fed into the triage/implement loop where a human decides each deletion (NEVER auto-delete; Chesterton's Fence; public-crate API surface excluded or deprecation-cycled). WORKFLOW FIT: run periodically at acceptance/UAT or on a cadence, reusing the `checks` module (already runs lint/format/test/mutation kinds in an isolated worktree) + the `review` entry mode; the deletion experiment maps onto the planned mutation module. This is `exploring`: the human directed (2026-07-19) recording it now and running the research pass AFTER the Q-51 Mealy exploration synthesises. A WebSearch-backed research pass is owed (lenses: a prior-art survey with citations; the concrete multi-signal design + `checks`/`review`/`mutation` composition; a skeptic lens on false-positives, the public-API/semver problem, and the auditor's own maintenance cost). Design record: `docs/plans/code-value-audit.explorations/`.

DESIGN PASS DONE (2026-07-24): four worktree-isolated explorers wrote `docs/plans/code-value-audit.explorations/Q-52-prior-art-survey.md` (prior-art, citations verified by curl against arXiv/dblp/GitHub/research.google because the harness WebSearch/WebFetch were down all run; the four security-venue debloating papers cited from knowledge, flagged not re-fetched), `Q-52-multi-signal-design.md` (the concrete report schema + `checks`/`mutation` mapping), `Q-52-skeptic.md` (adversarial), and `Q-58-ablation-design.md` (the folded Q-58 output-content ablation design). CONVERGENCE (all lenses): the report is ADVISORY and never auto-deletes, a human decides each candidate (Chesterton's Fence); build CHEAP-STATIC-FIRST and defer the expensive deletion experiment; that deletion experiment IS the reserved `Kind::Mutation` module (`src/checks.rs:94-95`, reusing `checks`'s isolated-worktree machinery), not a second mechanism; "nothing noticed" is necessary-not-sufficient (a candidate, never proof, and only relative to the named oracle set), so the report must carry a "not evidence of absence" caveat; the CLI/output/pack contract, `#[cfg(...)]`-gated, and FFI surfaces must be excluded before a human sees the report; churn x complexity is a RANKING (remediation) signal, not a deletion signal. RESOLVED divergence: the crate is a PURE BINARY (no `src/lib.rs`, no `[lib]`, all modules private `mod`), so there is NO downstream Rust library API and the skeptic's "structurally irreducible public-API false positive" largely does not apply here; the only contract to exclude is the CLI/output/pack surface, which makes the cheap static slice notably low-false-positive FOR THIS REPO. SHARPEST SKEPTIC CUT (Minimal by default): `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (already required pre-commit) plus rustc `dead_code` already cover the cheap private-dead-code case at zero marginal cost, so the incremental value of a heavier multi-signal tool is unproven; the skeptic recommends deferring the deletion experiment behind an EVIDENCE GATE (a measured count of cases where clippy passed but a deletion experiment would have caught real dead code). Status -> `open`: the design pass is complete and a human decision is owed on WHAT TO SCHEDULE (the cheap static report now vs defer-all-behind-the-gate) and, for the composed Q-58, whether to RUN the ablation now given its designer flagged oracle circularity (it can prove the RESUME STATE echo's value, V0 vs V1/V2/V3, but not the derived ACTIVE LOOP block's, whose next-action IS the oracle) and that the landed source-side fix already defused the acute 150 KB problem. Design records under `docs/plans/code-value-audit.explorations/`.

DECISION (human, 2026-07-24): schedule the CHEAP STATIC report now and GATE the rest. New step `code-value-audit-static` (86, not-started) builds only the zero/low-cost static report (rustc `dead_code` + `#[allow/expect(dead_code)]` markers + `cargo-machete` -> advisory `docs/plans/<task>.code-value-report.md`), excluding the CLI/output/pack contract + `#[cfg]`-gated + FFI surfaces and carrying a `not evidence of absence` caveat, never auto-deleting (Chesterton's Fence). New step `code-value-audit-deletion-experiment` (87, deferred) records the deletion experiment as the reserved `Kind::Mutation` module reusing `checks`'s isolated worktree, gated behind an EVIDENCE GATE: a measured count of cases where `clippy -D warnings` passed but the deletion experiment would catch real dead code (mirroring the Q-51 / Q-59 / Q-64 staged-behind-gates precedent). Chosen over defer-all (rejected: a cheap, low-false-positive win exists for this pure-binary crate, which has no downstream Rust API; Ground decisions in evidence) and over scheduling the fuller audit now (rejected: the deletion experiment is the expensive high-false-positive part the skeptic and the debloating prior-art both gate; Minimal by default). Serves Minimal by default (cheap slice only), Ground decisions in evidence (gate the expensive part, per-signal `file:line` evidence), Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff (reuse `checks` / `mutation`, one report), Structured data first, project for humans (JSON intermediate -> Markdown). Folded into `code-value-audit-static`, with the deferred `code-value-audit-deletion-experiment` sibling. Decision receipt `type:"decision"` `q_id:"Q-52"` in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`. Receipt: `Q-52`.
- `Q-53` (decided -> folded into `task-entry-regrounding`) whether to add a task-entry re-grounding and human alignment check before starting a step: DECIDED (Socratic, human, 2026-07-19) add a LIGHT, stakes-scaled task-entry RE-GROUNDING run before starting a step and on resume, sourced from the DURABLE artifacts (plan Step Detail by slug, ledger RESUME STATE, decision receipts by q_id, findings by path, code by file:line/commit) and NOT conversation history (a fact found only in ephemeral history is a durability bug to flush into the artifacts, not to cite; out-of-VCS history pointers were rejected as moving the fragility rather than fixing it): the orchestrator writes a short brief (what the task is, why it exists, the cited evidence including the decision receipt with the human's recorded choice, and what it is about to do) and pushes it for a go/no-go via the human-input contract, scaled to stakes. Also ADOPT structured PER-STEP PROVENANCE links (a step -> the decisions/findings/commits that justify it, mirroring questions' `folded_into`/`receipt`) that `render` can present as "why this step exists". Chosen over no-regrounding and over out-of-VCS history pointers. Decision and reasoning in `task-entry-regrounding`. Receipt: `Q-53`.
- `Q-54` (decided -> folded into `human-input-gate-reinforce`) the human-input contract (present options with their trade-offs, a recommendation, and reasoning judged against the numbered Project Principles, and let the human decide) lives once in `pack/AGENTS.md`, but the orchestrator drifted off it after a compaction and presented several decision gates as options-with-trade-offs while omitting the explicit recommendation and Principle-judged reasoning; how to prevent recurrence. This is control-drift (an agent forgot a rule that applies right here), not a missing rule, so the fix is point-of-action reinforcement. DECIDED (human, 2026-07-19): reinforce at the point of action via (a) strengthening `pack/prompts/orchestrator.md` so the human-input contract is an explicit per-gate checklist the orchestrator applies at EVERY decision presentation (referencing, not restating, the AGENTS.md contract, per Principle 8), built first as its own low-risk step; and (b) adding an awaiting-human-decision reminder to the Stage-1 driver `next` output (folded into the `workflow-driver` Stage 1 scope), which is the point-of-action anti-drift value the driver is designed to deliver, so this incident is live evidence for it (Principle 6). Chosen over folding the whole fix into Stage 1 (delays the recurrence-preventer), a note-only capture, and a deterministic check (the presence of a recommendation is not reliably machine-checkable). Decision and reasoning in `human-input-gate-reinforce`. Receipt: `Q-54`.
- `Q-55` (decided -> folded into `workflow-enforcement-tier`) the two-tier workflow enforcement gap (SE-3, from the `Q-44` architecture audit `docs/plans/architecture-audit.explorations/audit-sharp-edges.md`): W3 convergence, the metrics validator, and the drift guards only operate when a project opted into `--instrument` and has a JSONL log, so a NON-instrumented project gets NO machine enforcement of any workflow invariant and `validate --workflow` silently passes (a false green); the two-tier split is also undocumented in the scaffolded AGENTS.md, so a user reading the role prompt expects the same guarantees regardless. The audit rated this SIGNIFICANT. How to handle is an open decision; candidate handlings the human should weigh (not pre-decided here): warn on `validate --workflow` when no log exists; require the log unconditionally; or make round-logging core rather than opt-in, which the Principle 8 structured-source direction leans toward. Do not build until decided.

DECISION (human, 2026-07-31): FAIL WHEN `--workflow` CANNOT RUN. `validate --workflow` exits NON-ZERO when the check was explicitly requested and no metrics log exists at the resolved path, reporting why; plain `validate` (and `--source` / `--plan` without `--workflow`) is UNAFFECTED, an absent log there staying a stderr note and exit 0. The reasoning the human accepted: the user explicitly asked for the check, so silently skipping it and reporting success is the defect. Chosen over MAKING ROUND-LOGGING CORE rather than opt-in (rejected as forcing instrumentation on users who did not ask for it, and a substantially bigger change than the defect warrants; Minimal by default) and over WARNING WHILE KEEPING EXIT 0 (rejected because a warning with exit 0 is still green in CI, which is the actual failure mode). The break with today's exit code is authorised by Structured data first, project for humans, whose recorded 2026-07-18 rider makes the best long-term design win over backwards-compatibility at this pre-adoption stage and beat Safe on existing projects where the two conflict; Safe on existing projects is what makes the change `risky`, not what blocks it.

CORRECTION TO THIS ITEM'S OWN WORDING, recorded because the reproduction contradicted it. "Silently passes" above is an OVERSTATEMENT: the skip IS announced, twice, at `src/main.rs:845` and `src/main.rs:1001-1003`, and both announcements go to STDERR while stdout carries only the ok summary. The operative defect is the EXIT CODE alone, since a CI gate reads the exit status and not the stderr log. Read this as a false green, never as a silent one.

A SECOND DEFECT, NOT IN THE TEXT ABOVE AND WORSE, found by scaffolding a throwaway non-instrumented project and running the tool against it (2026-07-31). The metrics-log path resolves against the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY (`src/main.rs:429-431`) rather than against the plan source, so a run made from inside agent-scaffold against a foreign plan joined agent-scaffold's own 235-record log to a one-step foreign plan and reported `workflow invariants hold` at exit 0. Sharpened into a measurable FALSE PASS: give the foreign plan's step a slug that has round records here and mark it `complete`, and this project's rounds satisfy that project's convergence claim. The green is not merely empty, it is affirmatively wrong, and this is a straight bug independent of whichever tier policy was chosen.

SCOPE (human, 2026-07-31, receipt `q_id:"Q-55-scope"`): SAME STEP, SEPARATE INCREMENT. The defects are fixed by ONE step built as separate increments, so the path fix lands and is reviewed independently of the tier-policy change, with the path fix first so the tier change cannot hand users a directory-hopping workaround into the contamination bug. Chosen over giving the path fix its own step ahead of this one and over folding the pair into the validation-constraints step: the defects touch the same code path and produce the same user-facing green, so separate steps would mean reviewing the same region twice. Folded into `workflow-enforcement-tier` (order 94). The decision named TWO increments, which was correct for a step that was then two defects; the count is UNDER-SPECIFIED rather than wrong now that the scope has widened, and the second planner pass re-derived the set as THREE (the resolution rule and all its call sites; the containment refusal; the tier policy plus the documentation half), applying the same division principle rather than appending to the pair. Decision receipts `type:"decision"` `q_id:"Q-55"` and `q_id:"Q-55-scope"` in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`.

TWO SCOPE ADDITIONS, decided by the human after the first fold was authored, both of which that fold had explicitly left open rather than assumed. (1) The DOCUMENTATION half of SE-3 is IN SCOPE: the two-tier split is undocumented in the scaffolded AGENTS.md, so a non-instrumented user reads an unconditional promise of the `validate --workflow` backstop (`pack/AGENTS.md:93`) and, after the tier policy lands, meets a hard failure from a check the guidance still promises them. (2) The SIBLING COMMANDS are IN SCOPE: `status` (`src/main.rs:455-457`), `next` (`src/main.rs:479-481`) and the derived ledger path (`src/main.rs:1133-1138`) carry the identical CWD-relative defect. The fold's stated ground for treating them as separable, that a wrong path there yields an empty projection rather than a false assertion, was FALSIFIED by two explorers independently and re-verified first-hand by the orchestrator on main: `next` emits `state: converged`, `rounds: 2/5`, `next: mark the step complete, re-render, and commit` at exit 0 for a project with zero rounds of its own, and `status --resume` prints this repository's entire RESUME STATE verbatim into a foreign project's agent brief.

MECHANISM (human, 2026-07-31, receipt `q_id:"Q-55-mechanism"`): ANCHOR PLUS REFUSAL, IDENTITY QUEUED, closing a build-and-measure DESIGN PASS whose three records are at `docs/plans/workflow-enforcement-tier.explorations/`. Ship the metrics path anchored to the plan source PLUS a refusal for unsafe pairings, covering `validate`, `next`, `status` and the ledger path, and QUEUE project identity in the round record to the validation-constraints step. Chosen over pulling the identity fields into the same step and over shipping the anchor alone: the pass measured that anchoring alone leaves the DEFECT CLASS open (its own builder attacked its finished build and produced two further false passes, one via an explicit relative `--metrics` and one via a symlinked source, both printing `workflow invariants hold` at exit 0), so the refusal is not gold-plating; while pulling identity in would edit the record schema W3, W4 and W5 all read, which should be one deliberate edit rather than a rider on a path fix (Minimal by default, against Ground decisions in evidence). The plan-declared log path (`[meta].metrics`) is REJECTED, not deferred: its builder measured that it contributes nothing on shipping day, that a declared path reconstructs the same false pass in a worse form (CWD-independent, committed, and passing `validate --source` clean), that no validator can refuse it because the conventional log lives outside the plan directory so the declared ref must permit the `..` component `is_safe_sidecar_ref` exists to forbid, and that it cannot cover the Markdown `--plan` substrate at all.

THE CONVENTIONLESS-SOURCE CASE (human, 2026-07-31, receipt `q_id:"Q-55-noconvention"`): FALL BACK TO THE SOURCE'S OWN DIRECTORY when the plan source is not under a `docs/plans`-shaped root, with the containment refusal layered on top, over a hard error. The fallback was measured resolving the `--source myplan.plan.toml`-at-a-root case correctly, and Safe on existing projects favours resolving a legitimate layout over rejecting it. TWO ACCEPTED COSTS come with this choice and are NOT oversights to fix: a BARE FILENAME run from inside `docs/plans` remains a silent miss, which no containment guard can catch because containment is not correctness; and a SYMLINKED `docs/plans` directory becomes a FALSE REFUSAL, the canonicalising variant that would fix it having been measured to turn every printed metrics path absolute, changing output on the correct case. Receipt: `Q-55`.
- `Q-56` (open) the escalation-record schema refinement: a PROACTIVE human "converge-now" decision at a round was recorded as a `type:"escalation"` record, though the escalation record is nominally cap-only (it represents hitting the round cap and the human deciding to accept or resume). Whether a human CONVERGENCE decision deserves its OWN record type or a broadened escalation definition is an open design decision; candidates (not pre-decided): a new record type for a proactive human convergence decision; broaden the `escalation` record's definition to cover converge-now; or leave it and document the overload. This couples to the waiver model's `accepted-at-escalation` record-backed evidence, whose W5 join reads the escalation record, so any choice must keep that cross-substrate join well-defined. - `Q-57` (decided -> folded into `formatter-reflow-convention`) the treefmt / stash hygiene decision: every `scaffold-self` / `nix fmt` run reflows ~12-18 committed docs (and some `src/*.rs`), and writers stashed the reflow rather than commit it, so ~38 parked `git stash` entries accumulated. Root cause: the committed docs are not treefmt-clean, but running the formatter over them would hard-wrap prose against the human's stated no-hard-wrap preference. DECIDED (human, 2026-07-23): ACCEPT INCIDENTAL FORMATTER REFLOW. Incidental formatter reflow (rustfmt or treefmt reformatting lines a change did not intend to touch, for example after a scaffold regeneration or because a committed file was not formatter-clean) is ACCEPTABLE and is NOT a review finding; writers do not revert, stash, or `git checkout` it, and reviewers and triagers do not raise it. Chosen over the orchestrator's recommendation to format the code and exclude the prose docs from the formatter, and over keeping the per-hunk reverting (the status quo). The docs and prettier hard-wrap concern stays governed by the existing no-hard-wrap prose rule; this policy does not fix that, it only stops the reverting churn. Decision receipt: `type:"decision"` `q_id:"Q-57"` in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` (Q-57 is past the `Q-44` baseline, so W4 enforces the receipt). Decision and reasoning in `formatter-reflow-convention`. Receipt: `Q-57`.
- `Q-58` (exploring) whether `agent-scaffold next` (the driver's Stage-1 forward projection, `Q-51`) should PROJECT the current transient resume-state rather than VERBATIM-ECHO the ledger's `## RESUME STATE` section, and what output content best serves a resuming agent. It is meant to be a token-efficient resume aid but echoes that section verbatim: measured on this repo the output was 150145 bytes / 148 lines, of which the DERIVED ACTIVE LOOP block was only 799 bytes and the rest (~149 KB) was the verbatim echo of 27 dated `CURRENT TRANSIENT STATE` anchors, only 1 of which is live. A cheap SOURCE-side fix already landed (bound the `## RESUME STATE` section to the single live anchor via a `##` boundary heading, so the echo is now ~6 KB; the orchestrator keeps exactly one live anchor going forward). The deeper open decision (candidates, not pre-decided): (1) have the TOOL project only the current transient rather than echo whatever sits under the heading, so it is robust to source drift and not reliant on ledger discipline, which needs either the bounded source or the Stage-2 reconstructor; (2) make the transient resume-state STRUCTURED rather than human prose so the tool can project it drift-free (Principle 8, the restate-by-generation direction), noting the A-b Stage-1 decision deliberately chose verbatim-echo to avoid heuristic prose parsing; (3) determine the OPTIMAL output content EMPIRICALLY via an ablation: emit output variants (full; ACTIVE-LOOP-only; +current-anchor; structured-only), score a fresh consuming agent's stated next-action/constraints against a deterministic next-action oracle (derivable from the workflow rules, as the ACTIVE LOOP already is), and find the token-cost / task-success knee. This is `Q-52`'s falsifiable-deletion method applied to output CONTENT, so it composes with the `Q-52` code-value research. Do not build until decided.

DECISION (human, 2026-07-24): resolve the carrier mechanism EMPIRICALLY. Fold candidate (3)'s output-content ablation into the owed `Q-52` design pass (emit `next` output variants full / active-loop-only / +current-anchor / structured-only, score a fresh consuming agent's stated next-action and constraints against the deterministic next-action oracle the ACTIVE LOOP already derives, find the token-cost / task-success knee), and let that evidence choose between candidate (1) prose plus tool-side projection and candidate (2) the structured transient. Build NOTHING tool-side until the ablation reports; the landed source-side fix (the `##`-bounded single live anchor, ~6 KB echo) holds the line meanwhile. Chosen over committing to the structured carrier now (rejected: pre-empts the ablation that would prove structured-only wins the knee, and cuts against the fresh `Q-59` minimal-currency-signal precedent; Minimal by default, Ground decisions in evidence) and over projection-discipline-only now (rejected: leaves the transient prose and the real content question unanswered; Structured data first, project for humans). Grounds the mechanism in measurement not taste (Ground decisions in evidence), merges two owed research arcs into one (Minimal by default; Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff, revealed by the ablation rather than asserted). Fresh datum feeding the ablation: this session's self-contradictory prose anchor, corrected at commit `a949f34`. Status -> `exploring`: the ablation is the owed design pass that will resolve the carrier, composed into `Q-52`'s falsifiable-deletion research (design record `docs/plans/code-value-audit.explorations/`). The `Q-59` currency signal (checkpoint-commit / last-updated projected as current / N-commits-stale / tree-dirty) remains a required property of whichever carrier the ablation selects. Decision receipt `type:"decision"` `q_id:"Q-58"` in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`.

Keep the design record `docs/plans/code-value-audit.explorations/Q-58-ablation-design.md` on the shelf and RUN it only when resume-quality problems recur OR when the structured-transient carrier is actually being built, so the measurement informs a real build rather than a defused problem. - `Q-59` (decided -> folded into `resume-state-currency-signal`) whether the session lifecycle (the `pause` / `compaction-prep` / `resume` user-prompts) should be encoded as explicit, tool-validated STATES rather than the current prose-only checklists plus procedures. Current reality: `next`'s `LoopState` (`src/next.rs`) models only the review loop (ReadyToPlan, Blocked, AwaitingFirstReview, AwaitingFixes, AwaitingReviewers, Converged, Escalate, RiskClassConflict, Done); it has NO Active / Checkpointed / Paused state. `pause.md`, `compaction-prep.md`, and `resume.md` under `.agents/user-prompts/` are prose checklists, and AGENTS.md's "Checkpoint and resuming after context loss" section describes them as procedures. Nothing records "this session is checkpointed", nor validates that a resume follows a checkpoint, nor that work does not start while paused. The design space to explore (do NOT pick one, this is `exploring`): (1) where the state lives, a `[meta]` enum in `plan.toml`, or append-only `type:"checkpoint"` / `type:"resume"` records in `workflow.jsonl`, or a structured ledger field; (2) the command surface, a `checkpoint` / `resume` subcommand pair that writes AND validates the transition, versus validation-only where `next` / `status` read the state and refuse "do work" advice while checkpointed; (3) enforcement in `validate --workflow`, a resume must follow a checkpoint, no two checkpoints without an intervening resume, and the checkpoint commit must be clean. It COMPOSES with `Q-58` (tool-side structuring of the transient resume-state) and EXTENDS the `workflow-driver` step, so a design pass should reconcile `Q-59` WITH `Q-58` rather than bolt one on. Judged against the plan principles: P5 (make illegal states unrepresentable) and P8 (structured data first) are the drivers; P1 (prefer the cleaner long-term architecture) argues for reconciling with `Q-58`; P2 (minimal by default) cautions against over-building the command surface, which is why it is captured `exploring` (a design pass is owed) rather than built. DESIGN PASS DONE (2026-07-23): three worktree-isolated explorers wrote `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.explorations/Q-59-data-model.md`, `Q-59-command-surface.md`, and `Q-59-yagni.md`. They differ on how much to build now: a minimal currency signal (the YAGNI evidence position: no recorded transition failure exists, so build only a checkpoint-commit / staleness field) versus a fuller validation-only lifecycle state (session_state enum + a W6 transition-legality check, no commands). Now `open` for the human decision per the human-input contract. DECISION (human, 2026-07-23): Option A, the MINIMAL CURRENCY SIGNAL, fold the session-lifecycle state INTO Q-58's structured transient and build ONLY a checkpoint-commit / last-updated field that `next` / `status` project as "current / N commits stale / tree dirty"; DEFER the richer lifecycle state (a session_state enum, a transition-legality check, refuse-while-checkpointed) behind an EVIDENCE GATE (a first recorded transition failure), mirroring Q-51's staged-behind-gates precedent; NO checkpoint / resume commands; the state lives in the Q-58 carrier, not the instrument-gated JSONL. - `Q-60` (decided -> folded into `single-source-recommendation-rule`) whether the "Preflight" section of `pack/AGENTS.md` should explicitly restate that every option-set the orchestrator presents to the human carries a recommendation plus trade-offs plus reasoning judged against the plan's `[[principle]]` by NAME (the human-input contract), to make that standing directive concrete at resume time. - `Q-61` (decided -> folded into `uniform-agent-isolation`) the uniform-agent-isolation decision. DECIDED (human, 2026-07-23): EVERY spawned agent runs in worktree isolation (the strongest isolation tier the harness supports, tier order unchanged), and the orchestrator merges all their outputs onto main. This replaces the previous design where the read-only reviewers and the triager wrote their findings directly into main's `docs/plans/<task>.reviews/`: they now write those findings in their OWN worktree, which the orchestrator merges, and the cross-tree-readability and survival property is preserved because the merge puts the findings onto main. Two refinements: (1) when multiple agents run in PARALLEL (several reviewers in a round, or several explorers), the orchestrator merges their worktrees only AFTER they ALL finish (a batch-merge), never as-each-completes, so no interleaved partial state reaches main mid-round; a single non-parallel agent is merged after it finishes or converges as before; (2) the tool's emitted instructions must STATE this (the pack: `AGENTS.md` and the orchestrator / reviewer / triager prompts), not only the guidance prose. This SUPERSEDES the former "read-only agents need no isolation" carve-out and RESOLVES the explorer-classification inconsistency (explorers are read-only with respect to the reviewed product, since they author only advisory design notes and not the plan or the code, but they still isolate like every spawned agent, so they are no longer listed among read-only agents needing no worktree). Chosen over a narrow change to only the findings-writing mechanics, and over keeping direct-to-main findings. Decision receipt: `type:"decision"` `q_id:"Q-61"` in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` (Q-61 is past the `Q-44` baseline, so W4 enforces the receipt). Decision and reasoning in `uniform-agent-isolation`. Receipt: `Q-61`.
- `Q-62` (decided -> folded into `driver-isolation-reminder-scope`) the driver-reminder scope follow-up from `Q-61`. Now that the uniform-isolation rule makes the reviewers, the triager, and the explorers isolate too (not only the writers), should the `next` driver emit its worktree-isolation reminder at the reviewer / triager-spawn states as well, or is `spawns_writer` still the right scope? Currently `spawns_writer` (`src/next.rs`) returns true only for `ReadyToPlan` (spawns the planner) and `AwaitingFixes` (spawns the implementer), so the always-on isolation reminder attaches only at those two writer states; the review states (`AwaitingFirstReview`, `AwaitingReviewers`) carry no isolation reminder, and the content-pin test `the_reviewer_states_carry_no_isolation_reminder` pins that. When `Q-61` landed, the driver behaviour was deliberately left unchanged and a NOTE was added in `spawns_writer` flagging this as a still-open decision, because the isolation reminder there also carries the writer's resolved tier and its resolve-the-tier note, which concern the writer's product-content blast radius. Candidates (not pre-decided): (a) widen `spawns_writer` (or add a sibling predicate) so the isolation reminder also fires at the reviewer / triager-spawn states, matching the uniform rule at the point of action, and flip the pinning test; (b) keep `spawns_writer` as-is on the ground that the isolation instruction for the read-only agents is already carried by their role prompts (`reviewer.md`, `triager.md`) and by `AGENTS.md`, so the driver reminder need not duplicate it, and the driver reminder stays about the writer's tier echo; (c) split the reminder so a lighter isolate-in-a-worktree reminder fires at every spawn state while the tier-echo / resolve-note stay writer-only. Judged against the plan principles: P1 (one uniform rule, no drift between guidance and driver) leans toward (a) or (c); P2 (minimal by default) and the no-duplication direction lean toward (b). Do not change driver behaviour until decided. DECIDED (human, 2026-07-23): option (a), WIDEN the reminder to fire at the reviewer / triager-spawn states too. The future build widens `spawns_writer` (or adds a sibling predicate) in `src/next.rs` so the isolation reminder attaches at the review-spawn states (`AwaitingFirstReview`, `AwaitingReviewers`), and flips the content-pin test `the_reviewer_states_carry_no_isolation_reminder`. Reasoning: P1 wants one uniform rule with no drift between the guidance and the driver, and since Q-61 makes every spawned agent isolate, the reminder belongs at the point of action for the review-spawn states, not only the writer states. Chosen over (b) keep-writer-only (which leaves the driver silent exactly where an agent is about to be spawned) and over (c) split-the-reminder (extra surface for no clear gain here). This is a `src/next.rs` code change plus flipping the pin test, deferred as a build step rather than done in this fold pass.
