More importantly, the interval between them is not neutral: as set out under defect D, a tier policy without its qualifier leaves a non-instrumented user hitting a hard error from a check the guidance still promises them unconditionally, which is worse than the gap either change leaves alone. The mechanism documentation for inc1 and inc2 (help strings, the README anchoring note, the doc comments) travels with ITS increment for the same currency reason, and there is deliberately NO separate documentation increment: this project already carries a step about documentation currency, and shipping behaviour with stale prose beside it is the defect that step exists to remove.

THE ORDER IS inc1 -> inc2 -> inc3, AND EVERY EDGE IS LOAD-BEARING. The first planner pass argued that the path fix must precede the tier policy, because a user whose `--workflow` run started failing could "fix" it by running from a directory that happens to contain a log, which is exactly the contaminated green of defect B, so the tier policy would hand users a workaround into the worse bug. THAT ARGUMENT STILL BINDS, and the design pass GENERALISES it: the tier policy goes LAST because it is the only increment that makes a previously-green run fail, and EVERY escape hatch a user reaches for when it does is closed by an earlier increment. Standing somewhere else is closed by inc1. Passing `--metrics` by hand at a foreign log is closed by inc2, and it is not hypothetical: it is explorer A's second false pass and explorer C's attack 4, found independently on different models. Landing the tier policy before either would convert a quiet defect into a loud prompt to reach for the two workarounds that are still open. Inc1 precedes inc2 because the guard reuses inc1's root derivation, and because a guard without an anchor is candidate (b) standing alone, which refuses every cross-directory run until the user passes `--metrics` by hand, the objection the first pass correctly raised against (b) as an alternative.

## Risk classification

Each increment is argued on its own evidence. The first pass's "both risky" is NOT inherited; two of these arguments are new and the third has gained a factor it did not have.

`workflow-enforcement-tier-inc1` is RISKY (two consecutive clean rounds). It changes WHICH FILE the tool reads on every invocation of THREE commands that do not pass `--metrics`, plus which LEDGER two of them read, and the failure mode of a wrong anchor is not a crash but a confident wrong answer. The design pass measured that this failure mode IS SELF-CONCEALING: A's own build, correct on the reported reproduction, was still emitting `workflow invariants hold` at exit 0 on two other inputs until A attacked it deliberately, and nothing in the output distinguished the correct runs from the wrong ones. That is the same class of defect the increment exists to remove. It also COMPOUNDS FORWARD: after inc3 a mis-derived anchor stops being "reads the wrong file" and becomes "hard-fails a correctly instrumented project", so an inc1 defect escalates into a broken gate rather than staying a quiet one. The derivation additionally makes at least one SILENT JUDGEMENT CALL that no measurement settled (nearest-wins on a nested `docs/plans`), which is precisely the kind of thing a review round exists to catch. Relative-path handling is this tree's recorded weak spot rather than a neutral area: `is_safe_sidecar_ref` (`src/plan/source.rs:480-495`) exists because of it, and two backlog steps sit in the same family (`sidecar-ref-empty-string` order 63, `sidecar-ref-symlink` order 64). The counter-argument, that the eventual diff is small (A measured the anchor at `+79/-15` and the whole thing including siblings and ledger at `+163/-18`, mostly comments) and that there is a deterministic test for it, loses to the blast radius: every future invocation of the project's main validation surface, plus the agent-facing `next`, whose wrong answer is an instruction rather than a report.

`workflow-enforcement-tier-inc2` is RISKY (two consecutive clean rounds), and for reasons that do not overlap inc1's. It INTRODUCES a non-zero exit on invocations that succeed today, and it does so with a MEASURED FALSE POSITIVE already in hand (accepted cost (ii), the symlinked `docs/plans` directory), so it is a deliberate, knowing break of Safe on existing projects rather than a strict tightening. Its correctness property is a NEGATIVE, and the design pass demonstrated that a build satisfying the stated reproduction can still admit the defect class by two other routes, so passing the increment's own tests is explicitly NOT sufficient evidence here; the review has to include adversarial construction, which is what a second clean round buys. It is also the only place in the mechanism where TWO DIFFERENT RESOLUTIONS (lexical default, canonical guard) run against each other by design, and the disagreement between them is simultaneously the source of the guard's strength (it cannot be spoofed by a symlinked source) and of its one false refusal, so a reviewer who checks only one of the two has not checked the mechanism. The counter-argument, that it is roughly 80 lines sharing inc1's derivation, is about diff size and not about blast radius, which this project has already recorded losing.

`workflow-enforcement-tier-inc3` is RISKY (two consecutive clean rounds). It changes a CLI EXIT CODE, the most externally depended-on contract the tool has, and it is INTENDED to flip a currently-passing gate to failing for every non-instrumented project, which is exactly the population Safe on existing projects protects. That principle is not overridden lightly; what authorises the break is Structured data first, project for humans, whose own text records the human's 2026-07-18 decision that at this pre-adoption stage the best long-term design wins over backwards-compatibility and that it beats Safe on existing projects where the two conflict. AN AUTHORISED BREAK IS A REASON TO MAKE THE CHANGE, NOT A REASON TO REVIEW IT LESS. The boundary is easy to get subtly wrong in a way tests may not catch by accident: the `_` catch-all at `src/main.rs:999-1003` covers BOTH the TOML-source-present and the Markdown-plan-present variants of "metrics missing", and the fix must convert exactly those to problems without capturing a case that should stay a skip and without touching the no-`--workflow` path at all. THE FACTOR THE FIRST PASS DID NOT HAVE: this increment now also edits the SHIPPED PACK and regenerates two DRIFT-GUARDED deployed files, and its pack content is a COVERAGE CLAIM about an enforcement boundary. That is the one artifact species this project has calibration data on, and the data is bad: step 92 spent six rounds and fifteen findings on one such claim, all of them prose, zero mechanism defects, joint-third of seventy-seven artifacts ever reviewed against a project median of two rounds, with the ledger's own diagnosis being that "a coverage claim is unusually easy to falsify at an edge". The counter-argument, that the in-tree precedent at `src/main.rs:995-998` makes the code half a three-line change, is true and does not reach the other half.

## Acceptance check

Every claim below is a command with an expected exit code, so a round is settled by running it rather than by reading the diff. `Q-66` (reproducible evidence proportional to the claim, step `reviewer-reproducible-evidence`, order 88) applies: all four defects are behavioural, so EACH INCREMENT owes at least one test that is RED against the pre-fix build and green after, and the round report must state WHICH MUTATION or WHICH PRE-FIX REVISION produced the red. The red case for inc1 is the borrowed-slug false pass at check 4; for inc2 it is the explicit-relative-`--metrics` false pass at check 11; for inc3 it is the exit code at check 15.

BEFORE RUNNING ANY OF THIS: point `TMPDIR` at a directory OUTSIDE any git repository. Three of the suite's 386 tests (`checks::tests::a_non_repo_target_with_runnable_checks_errors`, `tests::init_plan_defaults_to_git_and_skips_inside_a_repo`, `tests::install_precommit_hook_skips_a_non_repo`) build a scratch directory under `std::env::temp_dir()` and assert it is NOT inside a repository, so a worktree-internal `TMPDIR` fails them spuriously. All three explorers hit this and all three correctly isolated it as unrelated to their changes. It is a property of the suite, not of this step, and this step does not fix it.

1. Build: `cargo build`. Suite and lint: `cargo test` (386 expected) and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, both clean. Plan render pinned: `cargo run -- render docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml --check`.
2. Rebuild the fixture from scratch (the command at the top of this file) and confirm `docs/metrics/` is absent: `ls "$SCRATCH/docs"` prints only `plans`.
3. AFTER INC1, defect B's original reproduction is dead: from the agent-scaffold root, `agent-scaffold validate --source "$SCRATCH/docs/plans/TEMPLATE.plan.toml" --workflow` does NOT read agent-scaffold's own log and does NOT print `workflow invariants hold`. Expect the stderr note naming the FIXTURE's own missing log path and exit 0 (the exit code is inc3's job).
4. AFTER INC1, the false pass is dead: rerun the borrowed-slug demonstration (fixture step `complete` with slug `triager-runs-only-on-findings`) from the agent-scaffold root. Before the fix it exits 0 with `workflow invariants hold`. After, no green. Give the fixture a log of its OWN with no evidence for that slug and expect the correct RED instead of the absence of a green.
5. AFTER INC1, `next` no longer fabricates: from the agent-scaffold root, `agent-scaffold next --source "$SCRATCH/docs/plans/TEMPLATE.plan.toml"` must NOT print `metrics: 235 records`, must NOT print `state: converged`, and must NOT print `next: mark the step complete, re-render, and commit`. Expect the fixture's own log (absent, or its own record count) and the state that follows from it.
6. AFTER INC1, `status` counts the right log: `agent-scaffold status --source "$SCRATCH/docs/plans/TEMPLATE.plan.toml"` reports the fixture's own record count (or `metrics: no log found`), never agent-scaffold's.
7. AFTER INC1, the ledger stops leaking: rename a fixture's plan to `agent-scaffold.plan.toml`, put a decoy `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.ledger.md` in the current directory, and run `agent-scaffold status --resume --source "$FIXTURE/docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml"` from the agent-scaffold root. It must print the FIXTURE's ledger or `no ledger at <fixture path>; nothing to resume`, and must NOT print any line of this repository's `## RESUME STATE`.
8. AFTER INC1, the conventionless source resolves through the fallback (`Q-55-noconvention`): a plan file at a project root with no `docs/plans` directory reads that root's own `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`, both from that root and from elsewhere.
9. AFTER INC1, NO REGRESSION ON THE CORRECT CASE, which is the Safe on existing projects check: from the agent-scaffold repository root, `cargo run -- validate --source docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml --workflow` exits 0 with `workflow invariants hold`, reading this repository's own log, and its three stdout lines are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-fix binary's (A measured this; a relative source must keep a relative printed path).
10. AFTER INC1, plain `validate` is unaffected: from inside the fixture, `agent-scaffold validate --source docs/plans/TEMPLATE.plan.toml` (no `--workflow`) exits 0 and prints the missing-log note on stderr. Same for bare `agent-scaffold validate` with no source at all, which has nothing to anchor to and keeps the CWD-relative path.
11. AFTER INC2, the explicit-relative-`--metrics` false pass is refused: from the agent-scaffold root, `agent-scaffold validate --source "$FIXTURE/docs/plans/p.plan.toml" --metrics docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl --workflow` exits NON-ZERO with the refusal naming both paths and the derived root. Before inc2 this prints `workflow invariants hold` at exit 0.
12. AFTER INC2, the symlinked-source false pass is refused: a symlink to a project's plan placed outside that project, with a full log sitting beside the SYMLINK, exits NON-ZERO rather than joining the symlink's neighbours.
13. AFTER INC2, a `..` escape is refused: an explicit `--metrics` that climbs out of the plan's root (for example `<root>/docs/metrics/../../../../../docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`) exits NON-ZERO, while a `..` that stays INSIDE the root is allowed and produces the correct W3 result.
14. AFTER INC2, the refusal is correctly SCOPED: it does not fire without `--workflow` (`validate --source <foreign> --metrics <local log>` still exits 0, since no pairing is asserted), and it does not fire on `status` or `next` at all, which keep their documented never-fails contract.
15. AFTER INC3, defect A is closed: from inside the fixture, `agent-scaffold validate --source docs/plans/TEMPLATE.plan.toml --workflow` exits NON-ZERO and reports the missing log BY PATH.
16. AFTER INC3, plain `validate` is STILL unaffected, which is the other half of the decision and the easiest thing to break by accident: re-run check 10 and expect the same exit 0 and the same stderr note.
17. AFTER INC3, the control still works, proving the change removed a wrong answer rather than the check: put an empty `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` in the borrowed-slug fixture and run from inside it. Expect exit 1 and the W3 message quoted above naming `triager-runs-only-on-findings`.
18. ACCEPTED COST (i) IS PINNED AS EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR, NOT FIXED: `cd <root>/docs/plans && agent-scaffold validate --source p.plan.toml --workflow`. After inc1 alone: the stderr miss note and exit 0. After inc3: a HARD FAILURE naming the path it looked for. In neither case does it silently read the project's real log, and in neither case is the fix to canonicalise the default. A test pinning this belongs in the suite so a later "improvement" that turns the default canonical fails loudly.
19. ACCEPTED COST (ii) IS PINNED AS EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR, NOT FIXED: a layout where `<root>/docs/plans` is a SYMLINK to a sibling directory is REFUSED under `--workflow` after inc2, with the refusal message. This is a known false refusal and the test asserts it rather than working around it.
20. AFTER INC3, the `SE-3` documentation half is real and checkable: rebuild the fixture WITHOUT `--instrument` and grep its `AGENTS.md` for the backstop sentence. It must now carry the instrumentation qualifier, and a reader of that sentence alone must be able to predict check 15's exit code. Then confirm the deployed copies are regenerated: `cargo test` passes, which includes the `agents-md-drift-guard` comparison of root `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.reference.md` against a fresh render, plus the `prompt-drift-guard` comparison over `.agents/prompts/`.

## Documentation impact

All in-repo, and each item travels with the increment that makes it stale rather than being left as a documentation step owed.

INC1:

- `src/main.rs:429-431`, `:455-457`, `:479-481`, the three `--metrics` help strings. Each currently describes a plain path with a clap-printed `[default:]`; after inc1 the flag is `Option<PathBuf>` with no `default_value`, so the `[default:]` disappears from `--help` and the help text must state the anchoring rule in prose instead.
- `src/main.rs:464-466` (`StatusArgs::ledger_fragment`) and `:482-484` (`NextArgs::ledger_fragment`), both of which say the default is `docs/plans/<task>.ledger.md`; after inc1 it is `<task>.ledger.md` BESIDE the plan source.
- `src/main.rs:1133-1135`, the `default_ledger_path` doc comment, which states the `docs/plans/<task>.ledger.md` convention, and `:1147-1151`, `run_resume`'s doc comment, which restates it.
- `README.md:212-224`, the `validate` example block, is where a note about the log being resolved relative to the plan source belongs. `README.md:226`, the `status` paragraph, needs NO change under the narrow refusal reading: its "Unlike `validate` it never fails on a missing or malformed file" claim stays true. If the wider reading of `Q-55-mechanism` is ever taken, that sentence is the one that goes stale, which is a reason to check it rather than assume it.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, the `## [Unreleased]` section. The section today has `Added` and `Changed` and no `Fixed`; check what a comparable fix did before introducing a new subsection.

INC2:

- `src/main.rs:438-440`, the `--workflow` help, whose closing sentence enumerates the error cases and gains the refusal.
- `README.md:210`, the `validate` paragraph, gains the refusal as a named failure mode, and `:212-224` gains an example or a note showing what it looks like. The deliberate break named at the end of "The two accepted costs" (a log deliberately pointed outside its own root now exits 1) belongs in the CHANGELOG entry.

INC3:

- `src/main.rs:791-816`, the `run_validate` doc comment, which states the superseded policy in as many words: "An absent file (the metrics log, or a `--plan` path) is not a validation failure ... a missing file prints a note to stderr and is skipped rather than hard-failing (the same treatment for both, so the behaviour is consistent)". After inc3 the treatment is deliberately NOT the same for both, and the comment must say why.
- `tests/validate_workflow_toml_source_needs_no_plan.rs:1-13`, the module doc, which frames the false-green rule as being about the plan source only, and `:96-98`, a comment asserting the soft-skip this increment removes ("with a source present but metrics missing the tool still soft-skips"). Inc3's new case is a sibling of the two already in that file and belongs there; inc1's and inc2's need multi-project fixtures and are likely new files.
- `README.md:210`, which currently says only that `validate` "exits non-zero if any exist, so it can gate a commit or run in CI" without stating that a `--workflow` run which cannot see a log is itself a failure.
- `pack/AGENTS.md:93`, the `SE-3` half. THE PASSAGE: the closing clause of the "Worktree lifecycle and merge-back" paragraph, "the deterministic `validate --workflow` check, once built, is the backstop that the required reviewed rounds happened before a step is marked complete". WHAT IT MUST SAY: that this backstop belongs to the instrumented tier, that a project scaffolded without `--instrument` has no round log for it to read, and that on such a project the check now REFUSES rather than passing, so the reader knows both that the guarantee is conditional and what they will see if they invoke it anyway. WHAT IT MUST NOT DO: restate `pack/instrument.md`'s schema, or re-explain the two tiers at length; the existing "When instrumentation is on" clauses at `pack/AGENTS.md:61` and `:63` are the established phrasing for this conditional and the qualifier should match them. Keep it to a qualifying clause; this project has five retrospective and one prospective confirmation that a fix pass which AUTHORS prose manufactures the next round's finding while a deletion-class pass does not, so the smallest true qualifier is the target.
- The two DEPLOYED copies of that render, root `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.reference.md`, must be regenerated in the same change or the drift guard fails. HOW: run the render half only, `cargo run -- scaffold --output-dir . --write --force --principles default --instrument`. Do NOT run `just scaffold-self`: `justfile:46-48` shows that recipe is the render followed by a repo-wide `nix fmt`, which the pack forbids an implementer, and this repository is not formatter-clean at HEAD. Skipping the formatter costs nothing, because the drift guard passes both sides through `normalize_wrapping` before comparing.
- NOT `pack/instrument.md`: its `validate` sentence ("exits non-zero and reports any malformed record") stays true, and none of its `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` references go stale, since the log still lives at that path INSIDE a project and only the resolution rule for invocations from elsewhere changes. NOT the role prompts: no prompt states where the log is resolved from. If the implementer does find pack text that goes stale, the deployed copies must be regenerated in the same change or the drift guards fail.

## Scope: what this step does not do

- It does not make round-logging core. That was the rejected option, not a follow-up.
- It does not add PROJECT IDENTITY to the round record or to the join. Decided as QUEUED to the validation-constraints step (`Q-55-mechanism`), with explorer C's build as the evidence and its three reported limitations as that step's inheritance. See "What this step does not fix, and where it goes instead" above.
- It does not add a `[meta].metrics` or `[meta].ledger` field. Candidate (d) is REJECTED with measurements, not deferred; see its own section.
- It does not extend the CONTAINMENT REFUSAL to `status` or `next`, which keep the documented never-fails projection contract, on explorer A's measured judgement. The ANCHORING does extend to them, which is what removes the fabricated instruction and the leaked resume block. The wider reading of `Q-55-mechanism` is raised for the human rather than assumed either way.
- It does not extend the EXIT-CODE POLICY to `status` or `next`. `Q-55` is about `validate --workflow`; the projections keep exit 0 on a missing log and report `no log found`.
- It does not fix the SILENT MISS or the SYMLINK FALSE REFUSAL. Both are accepted costs recorded above and PINNED by the acceptance check. A symlink-aware treatment, if ever wanted, belongs with the backlog step `sidecar-ref-symlink` (order 64).
- It does not change any check logic in `src/workflow.rs`. W3, W4 and W5 are correct; they were handed the wrong log.
- It does not fix the THREE TESTS that fail when `TMPDIR` is inside a git repository. That is a pre-existing property of the suite, recorded in the ledger as an orchestrator briefing defect and noted in the acceptance check so it is not mistaken for a regression.
- It does not settle the NESTED `docs/plans` case on evidence. Nearest-wins is explorer A's judgement, reported by A as such, and it is recorded here as a judgement rather than a measurement so a later reader can revisit it without having to rediscover that it was never evidenced.

## Success Criteria

- One command, run from any working directory and targeting any `--output-dir`, drops the minimal core (a usable `AGENTS.md`, a planning-document template, and the core prompts) into both an empty directory and an existing repository. Writes are off unless confirmed: a run previews the plan and only writes with `--write` or the selector's Save confirmation (`--dry-run` previews explicitly), so nothing is written by accident.
- By default it creates only absent files and never modifies existing ones; `--force` is required to overwrite; a default re-run therefore reverts nothing.
- The user can choose which principles and modules to include, interactively with sane defaults or non-interactively via flags or config.
- The dropped assets are immediately usable to run one pass of the workflow (plan -> review -> implement -> review) without further setup.
- Optional modules can be added without touching or complicating the core.
- The tool can scaffold from a user-supplied template pack, not only the built-in one.
- The scaffolded workflow is internally consistent: `pack/AGENTS.md`, the prompts under `pack/prompts/`, the README diagram, and this plan state the same rules the same way, and the convergence accounting (round outcomes and the single escalation cap) is deterministic and computable from the review ledger alone.
- The self-scaffolded copies stay reliably in sync with the pack: editing a `pack/` file and running a plain `cargo build` (no manual `cargo clean`) re-embeds the change, so `scaffold-self` and the golden sync-test regenerate from the current pack, not a stale embedded one.
- The human-interface layer is present: onboarding (a "Getting started, for the human" section that points to the editable kickoff prompt in `.agents/user-prompts/` and states the human's ongoing decision duty) and a single living human-decision queue that the orchestrator updates and pushes to the human at every checkpoint.
- The scaffolded workflow carries the human-input contract (every human-input point, escalation, intake, open questions, and clarifying questions, presents options, trade-offs, a recommendation, and reasoning judged against the project's numbered Principles, scaled to stakes) and the always-separate triager rule (the triager is a separate agent, independent of both the producer and the orchestrator, for every review round).
- The scaffolded workflow carries a git-durability-and-recovery discipline: a clean tree before spawning a writer, commit-before-delete for workflow-managed files, own-files-only formatting (no repo-wide formatters or cross-owner `git checkout`), an orchestrator recovery protocol on any kill or interrupt, and destructive validation in scratch. Every spawned agent (the writers and the read-only reviewers, triager, and explorers) runs under capability-tiered isolation (container if available, else worktree, else that discipline), and the orchestrator integrates their outputs onto main.
- Review findings flow through per-agent files that other agents read directly and the ledger references by path, so no finding is lost to orchestrator transcription; the files are committed before the orchestrator deletes them.
- A compaction-prep checkpoint keeps the plan and ledger authoritative for resuming after context loss: before a compaction the orchestrator flushes and commits the plan, the ledger, and the Open-Questions queue and verifies the plan's resume anchor, and on resume state is reconstructed from `AGENTS.md`, the plan, and the ledger.
- Human-invoked user prompts (the kickoff prompt and the compaction-prep prompt) live in their own `.agents/user-prompts/` directory, separate from the role prompts in `.agents/prompts/`, and stay thin triggers that do not duplicate workflow content.
- The workflow offers a human-invokable review entry mode (a fourth entry alongside implement, explore, and question-driven input): a human can review the whole tree or a diff against a named plan's Success Criteria, ad-hoc constraints, or open-ended correctness/quality, and get a committed findings report with a handoff into an implement task, reusing the same reviewers, separate triager, severity scale, and high/critical dismissal recheck as the other review phases.
- Optional verification modules compose on the core without complicating it: a deterministic-checks module (a user-configurable, pluggable lint/format/test/mutation gate over the code, with a read-only checks-reviewer, a `{{modules}}` guidance slot that is empty and byte-identical when no module is enabled, and an optional pre-commit hook), a test-driven module (a separate test-author role and a test-first two-gate profile) that hard-depends on it, and a mutation module that hard-depends on that.
- The scaffolded workflow's reviewer/triager diversity rule spans different models OR harnesses where available, so a user running multiple CLIs is guided to spread reviewers across them to reduce shared blind spots.
- The plan's live skeleton is a structured single source of truth: a `<task>.plan.toml` holds the Roadmap (step status, order, dependencies), the Open-Questions queue (id, status, one-line ask, a `receipt` pointer to the JSONL decision record, typed `folded_into`/`superseded_by` cross-references; the queue's `options`/`chosen` stay in the JSONL decision receipt, not the TOML), the numbered Project Principles, the step<->increment links, and (per Q-46) the exemption waivers nested on their step and the W4 baseline in `[meta]`; the append-only `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` holds only genuine events (rounds, escalations, decisions, intakes, dismissals). Typed cross-references replace the parametric status strings, so a `decided` question and a `blocked_by` step are structured fields, not prose conventions, and `validate --source` checks each resolves.
- `agent-scaffold render` generates a committed-but-never-hand-edited `<task>.md` from the TOML skeleton plus opaque Markdown prose sidecars, splicing each sidecar verbatim and never parsing prose back into structure, so there is no prose round-trip and nothing to clobber: render writes only the derived `<task>.md`, and a schema violation, an unresolved cross-reference, or a missing sidecar exits non-zero and writes nothing. A do-not-edit banner heads the generated file and names its real sources, and the derived Status line and the status vocabulary are generated (not hand-maintained), so they cannot drift.
- A `render --check` guard re-renders and compares against the committed `<task>.md`, catching both a hand-edit of the generated file and a stale render after a source edit; it warns locally so a forgotten re-render never blocks an in-flight workflow step, and fails hard in CI and in the pre-commit hook so a stale plan cannot land.
- Enforcement is preserved over the migrated data as a parser swap, not a rewrite: W3, W4, W5, and the pause.md catch keep working, reading `Step`/`Question`/waiver shapes and the baseline from the TOML and the escalation evidence from the JSONL, with per-increment convergence intact, the two evidence tiers un-launderable, and W5's record-backed join to a decision-scoped escalation preserved across the two substrates.
- New `round` and `escalation` records carry a structured step/increment id, and W3 and W5 join on it in preference to the lexical `leading_slug` strip for post-migration records, so the over-strip fragility (SE-10/B6) no longer applies to newly logged increments, while pre-migration records continue to join via the leading-slug shim.
- Migrating this repo is safe and reversible: the skeleton and sidecars are built additively while the hand-authored `.md` stays the live source (`[meta].primary = "markdown"`), validated synthetic-pilot-first, shadow-rendered and fidelity-diffed against the current plan, then cut over in a single `git revert`-able commit that sets `primary = "toml"`, renders, and (per Q-46) moves and prunes the historical JSONL waiver/baseline lines; `validate` stays green at every stage, and reverting the cutover restores both the hand-authored `.md` and the pruned JSONL lines.
- The scaffolded default stays coherent: a fresh `agent-scaffold` run drops a `<task>.plan.toml` skeleton, starter prose sidecar directories, and a rendered `<task>.md` that are internally consistent and `validate`-green, with no `w4_baseline` (so every decision the fresh project makes requires a receipt).
- The shipped pack's prompts and docs describe the same TOML+render+sidecar plan flow the tool actually implements: a freshly scaffolded project's `pack/prompts/*` and `pack/user-prompts/kickoff.md` describe authoring and editing the `.plan.toml` skeleton plus prose sidecars, rendering the generated `<task>.md`, never hand-editing it, and `render --check`ing before commit, with no residual Markdown-only-plan authoring instructions or stale `docs/plans/TEMPLATE.md` references; and the shipped `README.md`, `pack/AGENTS.md`, and `pack/instrument.md` are current with the render architecture (the README documents `render`/`render --check` and `validate --source`, and `instrument.md` documents that every metrics record, the `type:"decision"` receipt included, carries the required `task` field via its preamble).
- The workflow's control constants (the risk-class -> required-clean-streak map, the total-round cap, the backstop severity, the phase/tier orderings, the path templates) are single-sourced in `.agents/workflow.toml`, read by both `validate --workflow` and the driver from one `WorkflowSpec`, so the enforcement checker and the driver cannot disagree about the bar and there is no code/prose duplication (a built-in default equal to today's constants, pinned by assertion, keeps an un-migrated project byte-for-byte unchanged).
- The AGENTS.md control-constant fragment is generated from the same spec via a pack render slot and byte-guarded, so the prose statement of every control constant is derived from the spec the driver executes and the two cannot drift, while the rationale prose stays hand-authored around the slot.
- An advisory, read-only `agent-scaffold next` reports the current per-unit state, the valid transitions, and the next action as a filled instruction prompt (role prompt + artifact + diff range + findings/ledger paths + Principle reminders), in JSON and human text, recomputed statelessly from the plan + log + ledger + spec each call, and its forward projection of the convergence arithmetic matches `validate --workflow`'s backward computation on the same files.
- The driver is non-blocking in-loop (skipping the tool never deadlocks the workflow), consumes agent/human judgment only as typed inputs and never manufactures a verdict, and hard enforcement exists only via an opt-in boundary gate (`validate --workflow --strict` in CI or a pre-commit hook) at the landing boundary rather than per-step.
- Each canonical rule and constant lives once in `pack/AGENTS.md` and the pack prompts/docs point to it rather than restating it: the type-A copies the audit found (the total-round cap value, the clean-round counts and risk-class definition, the findings-file filename templates, the four-level severity scale and its absolute-rating gloss, and the isolation tier order) are replaced by references, the type-B role-scoped procedure prose is kept, and the two type-C accuracy bugs (the README W3-absolute waiver omission and the treefmt-v2 caveat's missing single owner) are fixed.
- Documentation currency is a core cross-cutting part of the workflow: the planner assesses which docs and prompts a folded change makes stale (stated in the planner duties and `pack/AGENTS.md` phase 2), the implementer updates them, the reviewer verifies, and acceptance carries a doc-currency check that a shipped change leaves no doc or prompt stale, with no new role or optional module added.
- The workflow performs a light, stakes-scaled task-entry re-grounding before starting a step and on resume: the orchestrator writes a brief (what the task is, why it exists, the cited durable evidence including the decision receipt, and what it is about to do) sourced only from the durable artifacts (never conversation history) and pushes it for a go/no-go via the human-input contract; and a step carries structured provenance links to the decisions, findings, and commits that justify it, which `render` presents as why the step exists.
